ai.description: Nanorana gammii is a 3–5 cm frog with a mottled brown or grey dorsum and yellowish belly. It is distinguished by a prominent, dark-edged supratympanic fold and granular skin on the flanks.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Nanorana gammii* is best distinguished by the presence of prominent, elongated, and often interrupted glandular skin folds on its back, unlike the smoother skin of similar species.
ai.habitat: *Nanorana gammii* inhabits high-altitude Himalayan streams and surrounding moist meadows, typically found at elevations between 2,000 and 3,500 meters.
ai.behavior: The Gammii frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates along the rocky streams and humid environments of its high-altitude habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Nanorana gammii* is an oviparous frog that breeds during the monsoon season (June–August), laying small clutches of eggs in high-altitude Himalayan streams.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Nanorana gammii* is endemic to the Eastern Himalayas, specifically occurring in the Indian states of Sikkim and Arunachal Pradesh at elevations between 1,500 and 3,000 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Gammii Frog produces a series of short, high-pitched "peep" notes, typically heard while calling from within or near fast-flowing mountain streams.
